groups.sentence: Instructors consider whether AI use would interfere with students' skill development when designing the course.
Instructors may restrict or prohibit AI where its use would undermine foundational skills or the value of human work.
Course assignments and goals are designed to build students' own skills, and AI use would undermine them.
Instructors explain to students why AI limits or use can undermine their learning.
Students use AI to support their learning and understanding, not as a shortcut.
Students do not use AI to replace the learning or practice that assignments are meant to build.
Students pause and consider whether their AI use supports or undermines their learning.
Using AI can replace, bypass or shortcut the practice and work through which students learn and build skills.
Overreliance on AI weakens critical thinking, problem-solving and other skills.
Students do their own work and thinking independently, without AI, to develop skills.
Struggle and effort are necessary for learning and cannot be skipped.
Writing is a way of thinking and learning, and outsourcing writing outsources thinking.
